column2: req_desc

Run manifest and health check
`/app/run.json` installs, builds and serves the app on port 4173 or `APP_PUBLIC_PORT`, and `GET /api/health` answers as defined in API.

Sign-in and sessions
Seeded staff sign in with email and password and receive an HTTP-only session cookie, and API calls without a valid session are refused, as qualified in API.

One error shape and order
Every API error uses the single error body and the single precedence order defined in API.

Server boundary
The server refuses cross-origin writes and oversized bodies and never serves source files, the run manifest or credentials, as defined in Server boundary.

Credentials from the environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment variables named in Configuration and secrets, never hard-coded in source and never sent to the browser.

Clock in and out on a rostered shift
A care worker signs in on a phone or unit tablet, clocks in to the current rostered shift and later clocks out, and sees the confirmation and worked hours on My shifts.

Clock-in window
Clock-in attaches to the caller's rostered shift whose window contains the current time, and clocking in with no such shift or while clocked in, or clocking out when not clocked in or after the clock-out window has closed, is refused, as qualified in Business rules.

One punch per tap
Repeated or concurrent punches with the same Idempotency-Key, or a double tap on the Clock in button, record exactly one punch, as qualified in Business rules.

Late after ten minutes
A clock-in more than ten minutes after the rostered start in Europe/London time is flagged late and waits for a manager's acknowledgement.

Real elapsed hours across clock changes
Rostered and worked hours are real elapsed time, so a 22:00 to 08:00 night is 11 hours across the October clock change and 9 hours across the March one.

Request leave
A care worker saves a leave request as a draft, submits it, and sees it in My requests with its status, hours and any short-notice mark.

Leave request lifecycle
A leave request moves only along the transitions listed in Business rules, and every other transition is refused without changing the request.

Notice period and short notice
A request whose first day is closer than the notice period in force, counted from today in Europe/London, is still accepted and is marked short notice.

Annual leave hours and balance
Annual leave costs the requester's real rostered hours inside its dates, fixed when it is submitted, and a request that would take the leave-year balance below zero is refused, using the balance defined in Business rules.

Withdraw before the first shift
A requester can withdraw their own request, an approved one only before its first affected shift starts, after which only a group HR admin can cancel it with a reason.

Own leave and sickness records only
A care worker who opens another person's leave request, sickness record or fit note by its id is answered as if it does not exist.

See the team rota
A care worker opens Team rota for a week and sees each colleague's shifts, with colleagues on leave or off sick shown only as away.

Rota fields per role
Rota responses carry only the fields published for the caller's role, so a care worker never receives an absence kind, leave type, sickness reason or balance, and managers see sickness ahead of leave in the absence kind.

Report sickness and upload a fit note
A care worker reports sickness, is asked for a fit note once the absence passes seven calendar days, uploads a photo or PDF, and later records their return.

Fit note required after seven days
A sickness record moves to fit_note_required once it spans more than seven calendar days, non-working days included, and cannot close with a span of more than seven days until a fit note is uploaded, as qualified in Business rules.

Fit-note upload checks
A fit note is accepted only as a PDF, JPEG or PNG judged by its content, up to and including 5,000,000 bytes, and its file name never becomes a storage path.

Private fit-note storage
Fit notes are kept in the private bucket under an opaque key and opened only through a 60-second signed link, issued afresh to the owner or a group HR admin, that serves the detected file type as an attachment carrying the original file name, as qualified in Services.

Work the approval queue
A unit manager opens Queue for their home, filters it, selects a request, and approves or declines it with the outcome shown in the queue.

Queue counts and filters per home
Queue items and status counts, filtered by home, status and week, include only requests from the homes the caller may see.

Who may decide a request
Only a unit manager of the request's home or a group HR admin may approve or decline it, and nobody may decide their own request.

Approval holds the floor
Approval re-checks every affected shift against current counts inside its transaction, so of two concurrent approvals that together breach a floor exactly one succeeds and the other is refused with the current counts.

Queue view in the URL
The queue's home, status and week filters and the selected request live in the address, so reload, a shared link, back and forward restore the same view.

Keyboard-complete queue
A unit manager can move between requests, inspect each strip cell, post cover, approve, approve with override and decline with a reason using only the keyboard.

Floor drop from preview to approval
A unit manager previews a request, sees which shifts would fall below floor, posts cover to each gap, sees the strip refill as bank carers claim, and approves.

Staffing preview
The preview endpoint returns 21 shifts with on-duty counts now and if approved, the floor in force, shortfalls and gaps, plus whether the request can be approved, as qualified in Business rules.

Strip matches the server
Each strip bar's height, its labels and the Approve button's state match the preview response for the selected request.

Breaches shown without colour alone
A shift below floor shows a hatched bar and its breach labels as qualified in Business rules, and all text and controls meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast.

Preview motion
Turning on Preview approval lowers only the requester's affected bars by one unit each, left to right 40 milliseconds apart, and turning it off reverses the change step by step.

Reduced-motion preview
With reduced motion requested, bars snap to their final heights with no stagger and every changed cell shows a before-to-after numeral pair.

Post cover to a gap
Dropping the Cover chip on a ghost slot, by drag or keyboard, posts one open cover shift for that gap, moves the request to cover_pending and shows the slot as cover posted.

Approve past a breach with a reason
Approve stays disabled while any affected shift would be below floor, and Approve with override approves only with a reason that is written to the audit log.

Claim an open cover shift
A bank carer opens Open cover, claims a shift at a home they are credentialed for, and then sees it among their shifts.

Open cover a bank carer can see
A bank carer sees and can claim only open cover shifts at homes they are credentialed for and for a skill they hold.

One winner per cover shift
Of simultaneous claims by different bank carers on one cover shift exactly one succeeds, and every other claimant is told it is already taken with nothing written.

Cover email without absence details
Posting cover emails each eligible bank carer once with the home, unit, date, shift times and skill, and never who is absent or why.

Run the home's day
A unit manager opens Today, sees on-duty against floor for each unit and shift together with the late clock-ins and missed clock-outs, acknowledges a late clock-in, and adds or removes a colleague on the rota.

Today in Europe/London
Every "today" the product uses, including the dashboard date, the default rota week, the notice count and the missed clock-out window, is the Europe/London date whatever the server or browser time zone.

Home-only picker and rota edits
The colleague picker, rota edits, Today totals and Today's late and missed lists for a unit manager include only their own home's staff and the bank carers credentialed there.

Set floors and leave policy
A group HR admin adds a future-dated floor version or leave-policy version for a home and sees it listed beside the earlier versions.

Effective-dated floors and policy
Each shift is judged by the floor version in force on its date, and each request by the leave policy in force on the day it is submitted.

Only HR edits floors and policy
A unit manager or care worker who tries to add a floor or leave-policy version is refused, as qualified in API.

Correct attendance
A group HR admin or unit manager corrects or adds a shift's clock times with a reason, and the change appears in Attendance and the audit log.

Corrections check the version
Every change to an attendance, the worker's clock-out and an acknowledgement included, raises its version by one, and of corrections based on the same version exactly one succeeds with one audit entry while every other is refused with the current record, as qualified in Business rules.

Append-only audit log
Each audited action writes one entry with actor, target, before, after and reason, and no entry can be changed or deleted through the API.

Watch holiday accrue
A bank carer works a claimed shift, sees their pending holiday accrual grow after clocking out, with a missed clock-out adding nothing until it is corrected, and sees a ledger entry once the pay period is closed.

Pay period close
Closing a pay period appends exactly one period entry per bank carer plus any adjustments, once, and a second close of the same period is refused.

Accrual arithmetic
Accrued holiday is 12.07% of real worked time in hours, with a missed clock-out counting as zero, rounded up at the fourth decimal place and never rounded down.

Export payroll timesheets
A group HR admin chooses a pay period and homes, creates a timesheet export, and downloads the CSV.

Timesheet CSV content
The timesheet CSV has the published columns and rows for the chosen homes only, leaves clock-out and worked hours empty for open and missed clock-outs, and neutralises any cell starting with =, +, - or @.

Stored exports and signed downloads
Each export is kept in the private bucket and downloaded through a 60-second signed link, issued afresh only to a group HR admin, that serves the CSV as an attachment named for its pay period, as qualified in Services.

Decision emails
Approving, declining or cancelling a request emails the requester exactly once, after the change commits.

Escalation after waiting
A request still submitted after the escalation delay moves to escalated and the home manager is emailed once.

Mail and storage outages
With mail or object storage unreachable, even at boot, every action still works, emails wait and uploads are held, and both complete once the service returns without a restart.

Visual identity
The screens read as steady, clinical and warm through the candle-wax page, deep teal floor line, hairline rules, equal-width numerals and type pairing described in Visual design.

Responsive layouts
Every screen works at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 without horizontal scrolling, arranged as described in Screens and layout.

Missed clock-out
An attendance left without a clock-out becomes a missed clock-out 4 hours after its rostered end, which counts zero worked hours, refuses a late clock-out, never blocks a later clock-in and is listed on the home's Today until corrected, as qualified in Business rules.

Removed shifts are gone everywhere
Removing a rota assignment takes it off the rota, My shifts, Today counts, previews, clock-in matching and the hours of later leave requests, cancels any claimed cover behind it, and lets the same person be added again, as qualified in Business rules.

One claim per retry key
A cover claim carries an Idempotency-Key, so retries and concurrent duplicates with that key return the one stored success and the same key on a different request is refused, as qualified in Business rules.

Sick days return holiday
Rostered hours of annual leave that fall on days the requester is off sick go back into their balance, and the same balance shows on /api/me, My shifts and the submit check, as qualified in Business rules.

One open attendance per person
Of clock-ins or clock-outs sent at the same moment by one person with different Idempotency-Keys exactly one succeeds and the rest are refused with nothing written, so a person has at most one open attendance and a shift at most one attendance, as qualified in Business rules.

Only published fields are writable
Every JSON write endpoint accepts only the body keys published in API, and a body carrying any other key is refused with validation naming each such key while nothing is saved.

Renames reach every surface, history keeps its names
After a person changes their display name every live surface shows the new name on the next read and the picker matches only the new name, while audit entries, stored exports and already queued emails keep the name as it was written, as qualified in Business rules.

Today counts stay true
Today's per-shift on-duty and senior counts always equal the staffing preview's counts for the same shifts, and its totals and summary line equal their sums, after every change to sickness, leave, cover or the rota, as qualified in Business rules.

Safe email headers
Display names with line breaks or non-ASCII letters still produce emails with one clean, correctly encoded Subject, the stored address alone in To, and no stall for the messages behind them, as qualified in Services.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve fields and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and nothing else is needed to start the app.

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree: runtime Python packages installed by install, plus npm ls --omit=dev --all --json or the lockfile's non-dev group if npm is used) and both typefaces, each with its licence.
Every shipped package and font uses one of MIT, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, ISC, PSF-2.0 or OFL-1.1.
The app stores state only in the provided Postgres database and MinIO bucket; no SQLite, Redis, other datastore or local state file.
The provided service configuration files and their seeded credentials are left unchanged.
Fonts and every other browser asset are served by the app itself, and no source file references an external CDN.
